children.translated_text: From true knowledge of the categories of means of knowledge, objects of knowledge, doubt, purpose, example, doctrine, members of proof, hypothetical reasoning, ascertainment, debate, disputation, destructive criticism, fallacious reasons, quibble, futile rejoinder, and points of defeat, there is attainment of the highest good.
Liberation is the successive cessation of pain, birth, activity, fault, and false knowledge, through the cessation of each immediately preceding cause.
Perception, inference, comparison, and verbal testimony are the means of knowledge.

children.text: indriyārthasannikarṣotpannaṃ jñānam avyapadeśyam avyabhicāri vyavasāyātmakaṃ pratyakṣam ||
children.translated_text: Perception is knowledge produced from the contact of a sense faculty with an object: non-verbal, non-errant, and determinate in character.

children.text: atha tatpūrvakaṃ trividham anumānaṃ pūrvavat śeṣavat sāmānyatodṛṣṭaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Next, inference, preceded by that, is threefold: from a prior sign, from a remainder, and from what is generally observed.
Comparison is the establishing of what is to be known from similarity to something well known.
Verbal testimony is the instruction of a trustworthy person.
It is twofold, because its object may be seen or unseen.
The objects of knowledge, however, are self, body, sense faculties, objects, cognition, mind, activity, faults, rebirth, fruit, pain, and liberation.
Desire, aversion, effort, pleasure, pain, and cognition are the sign of the self.
The body is the support of motion, sense faculties, and objects.
The organs of smell, taste, sight, touch, and hearing are the sense faculties, derived from the elements.

children.text: pṛthivī āpaḥ tejo vāyurākāśam iti bhūtāni ||
children.translated_text: Earth, water, fire, air, and ether are the elements.
Smell, taste, color, touch, and sound are the qualities beginning with earth, and they are their objects.
Intellect, apprehension, and knowledge are not different in meaning.
The non-arising of cognitions simultaneously is the sign of the mind.
Activity is the undertaking of speech, cognition, and body.
Faults are characterized by impelling activity.
Re-arising after death is rebirth.
The object produced by activity and fault is the fruit.
Pain is characterized by affliction.
Liberation is complete release from that.

children.text: samānānekadharmopapatteḥ vipratipatteḥ upalabdhyanupalabdhyavyavasthātaśca viśeṣāpekṣo vimarśaḥ saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Doubt is deliberation requiring a specific distinction, arising from the occurrence of common and multiple properties, from conflicting opinion, and from the indeterminacy of apprehension and non-apprehension.

children.text: yam artham adhikṛtya pravartate tat prayojanam ||
children.translated_text: That object with reference to which one acts is the purpose.

children.text: laukikaparīkṣakāṇāṃ yasmin arthe buddhisāmyaṃ so dṛṣṭāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: An example is that object concerning which ordinary people and examiners have the same cognition.
A doctrine is the established position accepted as the basis of a system.
It is fourfold, because of the distinct meanings of doctrines established in all systems, in a particular system, by implication, and by provisional acceptance.
An object that is not opposed to any system and is treated within the system is a doctrine established in all systems.
A doctrine established in one similar system but not established in another system is a doctrine established in a particular system.
That by whose establishment another topic is established is a doctrine established by implication.
Examination of a particular feature after accepting something unexamined is a doctrine of provisional acceptance.
Proposition, reason, example, application, and conclusion are the members of proof.
The statement of what is to be proved is the proposition.
The reason is what proves the probandum through similarity to an example.
Likewise, through dissimilarity.
An example, namely an illustration, is that which has that property through similarity to what is to be proved.
Or, through the reverse of that, it is contrary.

children.text: udāharaṇāpekṣaḥ tathā iti upasaṃhāro na tathā iti vā sādhyasya upanayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Application is the summing up, with reference to the example, as 'so it is' or 'it is not so' regarding what is to be proved.
Conclusion is the restatement of the proposition on the basis of the statement of the reason.

children.text: avijñātatattve arthe kāraṇopapattitaḥ tattvajñānārtham ūhaḥ tarkaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Hypothetical reasoning is supposition, for the sake of true knowledge, about an object whose true nature is not known, based on the plausibility of a cause.
Ascertainment is the determination of an object after considering the thesis and the counter-thesis.

Debate is the acceptance of thesis and counter-thesis, supported by proof and hypothetical reasoning, involving establishment and objection, not opposed to doctrine, and furnished with the five members.
Disputation is as just described, but involves establishment and objection by means of quibble, futile rejoinder, and points of defeat.
That, when devoid of establishing the counter-thesis, is destructive criticism.
The fallacious reasons are the erratic, the contradictory, the equal to the question, the equal to what is to be proved, and the mistimed.
The erratic reason is inconclusive.
That which, while accepting a doctrine, contradicts it is contradictory.
That from which consideration of the issue arises, and which is adduced for the sake of ascertainment, is equal to the issue.
What is not distinguished from what is to be proved, because it too is to be proved, is equal to the probandum.
What is adduced after the proper time has passed is mistimed.
Quibble is obstruction of a statement through the possibility of an alternative meaning.

children.text: tat trividham vākchalaṃ sāmānyacchalam upacāracchalaṃ ca iti ||
children.translated_text: It is threefold: verbal quibble, generic quibble, and figurative quibble.

children.text: aviśeṣābhihite arthe vaktur abhiprāyāt arthāntarakalpanā vākchalam ||
children.translated_text: Verbal quibble is the imagining of another meaning, contrary to the speaker's intention, in an object stated without specification.
Generic quibble is the imagining of an impossible object because of the connection of something possible with an overly general class.
Figurative quibble is the denial of the existence of an object when a figurative designation of a property is made.
Figurative quibble is simply verbal quibble, because there is no distinction.
No, because it has the status of a different meaning.
Or, if there were no distinction, because of some similarity all quibbles would collapse into one quibble.
A futile rejoinder is counter-opposition by similarity or dissimilarity.
A point of defeat is either contradiction or failure to understand.
Because of the varieties of these, there is multiplicity among futile rejoinders and points of defeat.
There is no doubt when one has ascertained common and multiple properties, or when one has ascertained one or the other property.
Nor is there doubt when conflicting opinion and indeterminacy have been ascertained.
And in conflicting opinion, because there is agreement.
And because indeterminacy itself is established in the very state of indeterminacy.
Thus there would be absolute doubt, because of the continued occurrence of those properties.

children.text: yathoktādhyavasāyāt eva tadviśeṣāpekṣāt saṃśaye nāsaṃśayo nātyantasaṃśayo vā ||
children.translated_text: From determination just as stated, because it depends on that particular feature, in the case of doubt there is neither non-doubt nor absolute doubt.
Where there is doubt, there this successive consequence follows in this way.
Perception and the other means of knowledge are invalid, because they are not established in the three times.

children.text: pūrvaṃ hi pramāṇasiddhau na indriyārthasannikarṣāt pratyakṣotpattiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For if the means of knowledge were established beforehand, perception would not arise from the contact of sense faculty and object.
If they were established afterward, the objects of knowledge would not be established from the means of knowledge.
If they were established simultaneously, because cognitions are restricted to each object, there would be no sequential occurrence of cognitions.
Because non-establishment in the three times is itself unproved, the denial is not tenable.
And because all means of knowledge are denied, the denial itself is not tenable.
Or, if that denial has validity, then there is no contradiction of all means of knowledge.
And there is no denial in the three times, because that establishment follows from speech, just as the establishment of a musical instrument follows.
And objects of knowledge are like the validity of a balance.
If means of knowledge are established through a means of knowledge, there follows the consequence that means of knowledge require another means of knowledge for their establishment.
Or, when that regress ceases, objects of knowledge are established just as the means of knowledge are established.
No; their establishment is like the establishment of a lamp's illumination.

children.text: kvacit nivṛttidarśanāt anivṛttidarśanāt ca kvacit anekāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because in some cases cessation is observed and in some cases non-cessation is observed, the reason is inconclusive.
The definition of perception is untenable because the statement is incomplete.
No; without contact of the self and the mind, perception does not arise.
The same consequence would also apply to direction, place, time, and ether.
Because cognition is the sign of the self, there is no omission of it.
And because non-simultaneity is the sign of the mind, there is no omission of it.
And because contact between sense faculty and object is the cause of perception, it is stated by its own word.
Also, for those asleep or whose minds are occupied, contact between sense faculty and object is a cause.
And by these, particular cognitions are designated.
Because it is contradictory, it is not a reason.
No; because of the superior force of a particular object.
Perception is inference, because apprehension arises from grasping one part.

children.text: na pratyakṣeṇa yāvat tāvat api upalambhāt ||
children.translated_text: No; because by perception there is apprehension even to whatever extent there is.
Nor is there only apprehension of one part, because a whole exists.
Since it is to be proved, there is doubt concerning the whole.
There would be no apprehension of anything, because the whole is not established.
And because holding and drawing are possible.

children.text: senāvanavat grahaṇam iti cet nātīndriyatvāt aṇūnām ||
children.translated_text: If it is said that apprehension is like an army or a forest: no, because atoms are beyond the senses.
Inference is not a means of knowledge, because it deviates in cases such as obstruction, injury, and similarity.
No; because, from partial trembling and similarity, there is the existence of another object.
There is no present time, because in the case of a falling thing, the times of having fallen and being about to fall are intelligible.
Those two also would be absent if the present were absent, because they depend on it.
The past and the future are not established through mutual dependence.
If the present were absent, there would be no apprehension of anything, because perception would be impossible.
But because the states of having been done and being yet to be done are intelligible, apprehension occurs in both ways.
Comparison is not established, because there is similarity in an absolute, predominant, or partial respect.
Since comparison is established from a well-known similarity, the stated faults do not apply.
Because what is not perceptible is established by perception.
When the gavaya is not perceptible, we do not see that comparison serves the purpose of a means of knowledge.
Because comparison is established through the concluding recognition, 'it is like that,' there is no lack of distinction.
Verbal testimony is inference, because the meaning is inferred from the non-apprehension of the object.
Because apprehension does not proceed in two ways.
And because of the relation.
From verbal testimony, due to the power of a trustworthy person's instruction, there is ascertainment of the meaning.
And because filling, burning, and splitting are not apprehended, there is no relation.
There is no denial, because the relation between word and meaning is established.
No; because the ascertainment of word-meaning is conventional.
And because there is no fixed rule with regard to a particular genus.
Its invalidity is due to the faults of falsehood, contradiction, and repetition.
No; those arise from defects in the action, agent, or instrument.
Having admitted it, the statement of fault is made with respect to a difference in time.
And because restatement is possible.
And because meaning is grasped from the division of the sentence.
Because utterances are employed as injunction, explanatory statement, and restatement.
An injunction is that which enjoins.

children.text: stutir nindā parakṛtiḥ purākalpaḥ iti arthavādaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Praise, blame, the deed of another, and ancient precedent: these are explanatory statements.
A restatement is the subsequent utterance of what has been enjoined by an injunction.
There is no distinction between restatement and repetition, because repetition of words is possible.
Because of repetition, as in an instruction to go more quickly, there is no absence of distinction.
And its validity is like the validity of mantras and Ayurveda, because of the validity of trustworthy persons.
The fourfoldness is not denied on account of the validity of tradition, presumption, possibility, and absence.
There is no denial, because tradition is not a different object from verbal testimony, and because presumption, possibility, and absence are not different objects from inference.
Presumption is not a means of knowledge, because it is inconclusive.
Because there is an imagined presumption where there is no presumption.
And the invalidity of denial is inconclusive.
Or, if that denial is valid, then the invalidity of presumption is not established.
Absence is not valid as a means of knowledge, because the object to be known is not established.
Since, among things that are characterized, uncharacterized things are characterized by the absence of that characteristic, those uncharacterized things are established as its objects of knowledge.

children.text: asati arthe nābhāvaḥ iti cet nānyalakṣaṇopapatteḥ ||
children.translated_text: If it is said, 'Where there is no object, there is no absence': no, because another characteristic is possible.
Because that is established, the reason is not valid with regard to uncharacterized things.
No; because establishment depends on the fixed state of a characteristic.
And because absence before production is intelligible.
Because it has a beginning, because it is perceptible by the senses, because it is treated as something made, and because of figurative usage.

children.text: na ghaṭābhāvasāmānyanityatvāt nityeṣu api anityavat upacārāt ca ||
children.translated_text: No, because absence in general, such as the absence of a pot, is permanent, and because figurative usage also occurs among permanent things as if they were impermanent.
There is no deviation, because there is a division of difference between what possesses reality and what is figurative.
Because of the qualification supplied by inference from a continuum.
Because the causal substance is denoted by the word 'part' or 'region'.
Because it is not perceived before utterance, and because no covering and the like is perceived.
The supposition of a covering follows from the non-perception of its non-perception.
There is no impossibility of a covering from non-apprehension, since the existence of non-perception is established from non-apprehension.
Non-perception is not a reason, because it has the nature of non-apprehension.
Because it is without touch.
No, because action is impermanent.
No, because atoms are permanent.
Because of transmission.
The reason is invalid, because the interval between them is not perceived.
There is no refutation, because of teaching.
There is no refutation, since teaching belongs to one or the other of the two positions.
Because of repetition.
No, for even when there is difference, the term 'repetition' is used figuratively.

children.text: anyat anyasmāt ananyatvāt ananyat iti anyatābhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What is other is other than another because it is not non-other; thus 'non-other' means the absence of otherness.
When that is absent, there is no non-otherness of the two, since each is established in dependence on the other.
Because no cause of destruction is perceived.
Since no cause of non-hearing is perceived, there would be the consequence of constant hearing.
And when something is being perceived, non-perception does not exist; therefore it is not an adequate designation.
Because of conjunction caused by the hand, there is no non-perception when sound is absent.
And if no cause of destruction is perceived and the thing remains, the consequence would be its permanence.
Because it is without touch, there is no refutation.
And because another case-ending is possible in a compound.
There is doubt, because alteration and substitution are taught.
When the original is enlarged, the alteration is enlarged.
The reason is invalid for alterations, because smaller, equal, and larger forms are observed.
Since both kinds of reason are absent, the example does not prove the thesis.
No, because there is variation of alteration among things whose originals are not alike.
Like the inequality in transformations of substances, alteration of phonemes lacks uniformity.
No, because the properties of an alteration are not applicable.
Because things that have undergone alteration do not return again.
The reason is invalid, because gold and the like do return.
No, because their alterations are not separate from the state of being gold.
Because they are not separate from being phonemes, the alteration of phonemes is not refuted.
The connection with a property belongs to what possesses a universal, not to the universal itself.
If they are permanent there is no alteration, and if they are impermanent they do not endure.

children.text: nityānām atīndriyatvāt taddharmavikalpāt ca varṇavikārāṇām apratiṣedhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because permanent things are beyond the senses, and because there may be variation in their properties, alteration of phonemes is not refuted.
And if they are unstable, then alteration of them is possible, just as the perception of phonemes is possible.
If they possess the property of alteration, permanence is absent; and because alteration at another time is possible, there is no refutation.
Because there is no fixed rule concerning the original.
If there is a rule within irregularity, it is not irregularity.
Because rule and irregularity are contradictory, and because a rule may exist in irregularity, there is no refutation.
But the alterations of phonemes are possible through acquisition of another quality, suppression, diminution, increase, and coalescence.
A word is those phonemes ending in an inflectional ending.
There is doubt, because figurative usage occurs through the proximity of individual, form, and universal.
An individual is that to which the figurative usages of a word-aggregate, abandonment, acceptance, number, increase, decrease, color, compound, and connection are applied as explicit usages.
No, that is not so, because it does not endure.

Because of accompaniment, location, purpose, conduct, measure, support, proximity, conjunction, means, and mastery, there is figurative application of a term even where the thing is not actually that, as in the cases of a brāhmaṇa, a platform, a cart, a king, barley-meal, sandalwood, the Gaṅgā, a garment, food, and a man.
Form is so called because the establishment of the arrangement of beings depends on it.

children.text: vyaktyākṛtiyukte api aprasaṅgāt prokṣaṇādināṃ mṛdgavake jātiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even where an individual and a form are present, rites such as sprinkling do not apply to a clay cow; therefore the universal is the referent.
No, because the manifestation of the universal depends on form and individual.
But individual, form, and universal are the meaning of a word.
An individual is a concrete form that is the locus of particular qualities.
Form is that which is called the mark of the universal.
A universal has the nature of producing the same cognition.
Because one and the same object is grasped by sight and touch.
No, because the fields of the senses are fixed.
Precisely because that fixed order exists, the existence of the self is not refuted.
Because there is no sin in burning a body.
That absence remains even in burning something with a self, because the self is permanent.
No, because what is killed is the agent who is the locus of effects.
Because what is seen by the left eye is recognized by the other.
No, because the notion of duality arises from there being two in one place, separated by the nasal bone.
There is no unity, because when one is destroyed the second is not destroyed.
The reason is invalid, because the whole is perceived even when a part is destroyed.
Because it conflicts with the example, there is no refutation.
Because of a modification in another sense faculty.
No, because memory has as its object what is to be remembered.
Because that quality of the self exists, there is no refutation.
No, because the causes for apprehending the self cannot exist in the mind alone.
Since an instrument of knowledge for the knower is possible, it is merely a difference of designation.
And the restriction is without inference.
Because a newborn's apprehension of joy, fear, and sorrow follows from the connection with memories of former practice.
That modification is like the opening and closing modifications in lotuses and the like.
No, because the modifications of things composed of five elements are caused by heat, cold, rain, and season.
Because the desire for breast milk is produced by the practice of taking food after death.
Its approach is like the movement of iron toward a magnet.
No, because activity is absent elsewhere.
Because birth among those free from passion is not observed.
Its production is like the production of a substance together with qualities.
No, because passion and the like have intention as their cause.
It is earthy, because another quality is apprehended.
It is earthy, watery, and fiery, because the qualities belonging to these are apprehended.
It is four-elemental, because inhalation and exhalation are apprehended.
It is five-elemental, because of smell, moisture, cooking or digestion, configuration, and the giving of space.
And because of the authority of scripture.

children.text: kṛṣṇasāre sati upalambhāt vyatiricya ca upalambhāt saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When there is the black antelope skin there is doubt, since there is apprehension in its presence and apprehension apart from it.
Because great and minute things are apprehended.
Their apprehension is due to a particular contact between the ray and the object.
Because that is not apprehended, it is not a reason.
The non-apprehension by perception of what is being inferred is not a reason for its non-existence.
And the restriction of apprehension is due to the difference between substance, quality, and property.
The apprehension of color is due to inherence in many substances and also to a particular color.
And the arrangement of the sense organs, produced by action, depends on the purpose of the person.
Its non-apprehension is like the non-apprehension of the light of a meteor at midday.
No, because there is non-apprehension even at night.
Since objects are apprehended with the assistance of external light, non-apprehension is due to non-manifestation.
And when there is manifestation, it is because of being overpowered.
And because the eye-rays of night-wanderers are seen.
There is apprehension without reaching, because things separated by glass, mica, a film, or crystal are apprehended.
There is no refutation, because things separated by a wall are not apprehended.
Because there is no obstruction, contact is possible.
For the sun-ray is not impeded even when a combustible object is separated by crystal.
No, because there would follow an unwarranted transfer of each one's properties to the other.
Color is apprehended in a mirror and in water because clarity is their nature.
For injunction and prohibition concerning things seen and inferred are not possible.
There is doubt because, when the place is different, there is plurality, and because a whole cannot occupy many places.
Because there is no separation from the skin.
No, because objects are not apprehended simultaneously.
And because of contradiction, the skin is not a single sense organ.
Because there are five sense objects.
No, because its objects are many.
Because there is no separation from smell-ness and the rest, smell and the others are not denied.
Because there is no difference in being an object, there is unity.
No, because of the fivefold distinction in the mark of cognition, substrate, movement, form, and class.
There is identity because the distinctive qualities of the elements are apprehended.
Smell, taste, color, touch, and sound, ending with touch, belong to earth.
For water, fire, and air, each earlier quality is successively excluded, and for ether the later one remains.
No, because all qualities are not apprehended.
Because each later quality is absent one by one, the later and later substances lack apprehension of that quality.
For the lower is pervaded by the higher.
No, because earth and water are perceptible.
Because each preceding quality is predominant, each corresponding element is primary.
But its determinate standing is because of preponderance.
Because the sense organs possess qualities.
And because, for that very reason, that is not apprehended by it.
No, because the quality of sound is apprehended.
Its apprehension is due to dissimilarity from the qualities of other substances.
There is doubt because of similarity to action and ether.
Because the object is recognized again.
Because it is equal to what is to be proved, it is not a reason.
No, because there is no simultaneous apprehension.
And if there were no recognition, destruction would follow.
Because it occurs in sequence, apprehension is not simultaneous.
And non-recognition is due to the mind being occupied with another object.
No, because there is no motion.
The supposition that it is different is like the supposition of difference in crystal.

children.text: sphaṭike api aparāparotpatteḥ kṣaṇikatvāt vyaktīnām ahetuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even in crystal, since individuals arise one after another and are momentary, this is not a reason.
In the absence of a determining reason, admission is according to observation.
No, because the causes of origination and destruction are apprehended.
Its origination is like the origination of curd, and like the non-apprehension of causes at the destruction of milk.
Since it is apprehended from an inferential mark, it is not non-apprehension.
No, because another quality, transformation, appears from milk.
The observed origination of another substance from another configuration is the inference of the cessation of the previous substance.

children.text: kvacit vināśakāraṇānupalabdheḥ kvacit ca upalabdheḥ anekāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because in some cases the cause of destruction is not apprehended and in some cases it is apprehended, the reason is inconclusive.
No, because cognition remains even when that destruction of the sense organ and object occurs.
And because cognitions are not apprehended simultaneously, this does not apply to the mind.
Even if that is a quality of the self, the same point applies.
Because the mind has no contact with the senses, that cognition does not arise.
No, because no cause of origination has been specified.
And because no cause of destruction is apprehended, if it remains there would follow its eternality.
Because cognition is known to be impermanent, its destruction comes from another cognition, as in the case of sound.

children.text: jñānasamavetātmapradeśasannikarṣāt manasaḥ smṛtyutpatteḥ na yugapat utpattiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because memory arises from the contact of the mind with the region of the self in which cognition inheres, there is no simultaneous origination.
No, because the mind operates inside the body.
Because it is what is to be proved, it is not a reason.
There is no denial, because the maintenance of the body is possible while one is remembering.
No, because the mind moves swiftly.
No, because the time of remembering is not fixed.
And because of prompting by the self, chance, and cognition, there is no special conjunction.
This is the same as the special conjunction in the case of a person whose mind is occupied and who feels pain in the foot.
Because acts of attention, signs, and other cognitions do not occur simultaneously, remembering is not simultaneous.
Because, for the knower, undertaking and ceasing have desire and aversion as their causes.
Because they are marks of that, there is no denial of desire and aversion in earth and the other elements.
Because undertaking and ceasing are seen in axes and the like.
But regularity and irregularity are what distinguish that case.
Because it has the reasons stated above, because it is dependent, and because what has not been done would come to one, it is not the mind.
It follows by elimination, and because the reasons stated above are established.
But memory belongs to the self, because knowing is its own nature.

It arises from causes such as attention, fixation, repeated practice, a sign, a mark, similarity, possession, relation of support and supported, immediate sequence, separation, having one effect, opposition, excess, attainment, intervention, pleasure, pain, desire, aversion, fear, need, action, attachment, merit, and demerit.
Because action is apprehended as non-abiding.
Indistinct apprehension occurs because of non-abidingness, like the indistinct apprehension of color in a flash of lightning.
By supplying a reason, what is to be denied is admitted.
No; its apprehension is like the apprehension of a continuous series of lamp flames becoming manifest.
There is doubt about substance, because one's own qualities and another's qualities are apprehended in it.
Because color and the other qualities persist as long as the body does.
No, because another cooked quality is produced.
Since an opposite is established, there is no denial of the cooked qualities.
Because it pervades the body.
No, because it is not apprehended in hair, nails, and the like.
Since the body extends only as far as the skin, the consequence does not apply to hair, nails, and the like.
Because it is unlike the qualities of the body.
No, because color and the other qualities are mutually dissimilar.
Because color and the other qualities are sense-perceptible, there is no denial.
Because cognitions are not simultaneous, the mind is one.
No, because many actions are apprehended at once.
Its apprehension is like the sight of a firebrand circle, because of rapid movement.
And because it has the reasons stated above, it is atomic.
Its origination results from the connection with the fruit of what was previously done.
Its material cause is from the elements, as bodily form has its material cause from them.
No, because it is equal to what is to be proved.
No, because mother and father are causes of origination.
So too is food.
And because, when there is attainment, there is no fixed rule.
Action is the cause of the production of conjunction, just as it is the cause of the production of the body.
By this, the absence of a fixed rule has been answered.

children.text: tat adṛṣṭakāritam iti cet punaḥ tatprasaṅgaḥ apavarge ||
children.translated_text: If one says that it is made by the unseen, then the same consequence arises again in liberation.
And because it has the mind's action as its cause, there would be no cessation of conjunction.
And eternality would follow, because death would be impossible.
This may be like the atomic dark color and its non-eternality.
No, because there would be the consequence that what was not done comes to one.
Activity is as described above.
So too are the defects.
There is a threefold grouping, because the objects of attachment, aversion, and delusion are included.
No, because there is a single opposed condition.
Because of deviation, it is not a reason.
Among them delusion is worse, because the others do not arise in one who is not deluded.
Because of the relation of cause and caused, there is a difference in object from the defects.
No, because delusion is included within the definition of defect.
And because the relation of cause and caused is established, there is no denial in the case of things of the same kind.
If the self is eternal, post-mortem existence is established.
Manifest things come from the manifest, because perception is authoritative.
No, because a pot does not arise from a pot.
There is no denial of a pot's arising from the manifest.
Existence arises from nonexistence, because manifestation does not occur without destroying what was before.
Because of contradiction, the expression is not applicable.
No, because causal words are used for the past and the future.
No, because there is no production from things that have perished.
There is no denial, because the sequence is specified.
<s>Īśvara</s> is the cause, because the fruitlessness of human action is observed.
No, because in the absence of human action, fruits do not arise.
Because it is caused by that, this is not a reason.
Things arise without a cause, because sharpness in thorns and the like is observed.
Because the causeless would be a cause, things do not arise without a cause.
Since cause and non-cause are different objects, there is no denial.
Everything is impermanent, because it has origination and destruction as its properties.
No, because impermanence itself would be impermanent.
Its impermanence is like something burnable by fire, or like the destruction of what is destructible along with it.
The eternal is not rejected, because things stand according to apprehension.
Everything is eternal, because the five elements are eternal.
No, because causes of origination and destruction are apprehended.
Because it is included within that definition, there is no denial.
No, because origination and its cause are apprehended.
No, because orderly determination would be impossible.
Everything is separate, because separateness is a defining mark of entities.
No, because one entity is produced by many defining marks.
There is no denial precisely because the defining marks are ordered.
Everything is absence, because mutual absence is established among entities.
No, because entities are established by their own nature.
Own-nature is not established, because it is relational.
Because it is contradictory, this is unreasonable.
The absolute claim about number is not established, both because the cause is not established and because it is established.
No, because the parts of the cause are absent.
Because it is without parts, this is not a reason.
There is doubt because the fruit is produced immediately and at a later time.
No, because it is to be enjoyed immediately and at a later time.
Destruction is the reason for non-production after an interval.
Before production, it may be so, like the fruit of a tree.
It is not nonexistent, not existent, not both existent and nonexistent, because existent and nonexistent things are dissimilar.
Because production and disappearance are observed.
But that nonexistent thing is established by cognition.
Because of the difference of substrate, the comparison with the production of tree-fruit is not a reason.
There is no denial, because pleasure rests in the self.
No, because fruits such as sons, cattle, wife, servants, gold, food, and the like are specified.
Because fruit is produced in relation to them, the figurative usage treats them as fruit-bearing.
Because it is connected with various afflictions, birth and origination are only suffering.
No, because pleasure too arises in the intervals.
There is no denial, because obstruction has not ceased and because, for one who feels, there is the fault of seeking.
And because, when pain is differentiated, there is the conceit of pleasure.
Because of the continuation of debt, affliction, and activity, there would be no liberation.
Because the primary word is not appropriate, it is a restatement by means of a secondary word, since blame and praise are appropriate.
There is no denial with respect to the self, because of superimposition.
And because the conclusion that the vessel-piling sacrifice has an end is not appropriate, there is no absence of fruit.
For one in deep sleep, since dreams are not seen and afflictions are absent, there is liberation.
No; activity does not serve rebirth for one whose afflictions are weakened.
No, because the continuity of afflictions is natural.
Even if it is natural, there is impermanence, as in the impermanence of prior non-existence before origination.
Or as in the impermanence of the dark color of an atom.
And no, because passion and the rest have conception as their cause.
From true knowledge there is the cessation of egoism, the cause of the defects.
The objects, color and the rest, made by conception, are the causes of the defects.
But the cause of that is the conceit regarding an aggregate whole.
There is doubt because knowledge and ignorance are twofold.
There is no doubt about that, because the preceding reason is established.
Then, because its occurrence is also not appropriate, there would be no doubt.
Because the parts occur in the whole and in one portion, there is the state of being a whole made of parts.
And if it did not occur in them, there would be no whole made of parts.
And because it does not occur apart from the parts.
Nor are the parts identical with the whole.
Since in one thing there is no difference, and since use of the word “difference” would be inappropriate, the question does not arise.
Even if there is another part, non-occurrence is not a reason.
Its apprehension is like the apprehension of a mass of hairs by a person with diseased vision.

Because the sense organ does not overstep its own object, and because apprehension of the object is thus sharp or dull according to the condition of the sense, there is no activity toward a non-object.
And in this way there is the consequence of parts and wholes extending up to dissolution.
No; there is no dissolution, because atoms exist.
Or the ultimate limit is the minute particle.
Because of the interpenetration of ether, that is not appropriate.
Or ether would not be all-pervading.
Because another cause is stated for produced substances, inside and outside, that is absent in what is unproduced.
And because sound, conjunction, and separation are manifested, it is all-pervading.
Non-displacement, non-obstruction, and pervasiveness are properties of ether.
And because configuration is appropriate for embodied things, parts exist.
And because conjunction is appropriate.
There is no denial, because it would create infinite regress and because infinite regress is not appropriate.

children.text: buddhyā vivecanāttu bhāvānāṃ yāthātmyānupalabdhistantvapakarṣaṇe paṭasadbhāvānupalabdhivat tadanupalabdhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: But from analytical discrimination by the intellect there is non-apprehension of things in their true nature, just as when threads are pulled away there is non-apprehension of the existence of the cloth; so there is non-apprehension of that.
Because it is contradictory, it is not a reason.
Because it depends on that, it is not apprehended separately.
And because an object is understood through a means of knowledge.
Through the non-appropriateness and appropriateness of means of knowledge.
This conceit about means of knowledge and objects of knowledge is like conceit about dream objects.
Or like magic, a city of the Gandharvas, or a mirage.
Because there is no reason, it is not established.
And the conceit about dream objects is like memory and conception.
The destruction of false apprehension comes from true knowledge, as the destruction of conceit about dream objects occurs on awakening.
And this is so for cognition also, because the existence of its cause is apprehended.
And because there is a distinction between what is grounded in reality and what is primary, the twofold nature of false cognition is appropriate.
Through practice of a special kind of concentration.
No, because of the strength of particular objects.
And because one is set in motion by hunger and the like.
Its arising is due to the continuation of the fruit of former action.
Instruction in the practice of yoga is given in forests, caves, riverbanks, and the like.
The same consequence would apply even in liberation.
No, because what has been accomplished must necessarily occur.
And that is absent in liberation.
For that purpose, through the practice of restraints and observances, through cultivation of the self, and through yoga, one proceeds by the means of knowledge of the self.
There is practice in grasping knowledge, and discussion with those who know that science.
One should enter into that with pupils, teachers, fellow students, and those distinguished persons who seek the highest good and are free from envy.
Or even with an opponent, if there is a purpose and a desire for the object.
For the protection of ascertainment of truth, eristic debate and destructive criticism are used, like a covering of thorn-branches for the protection of the sprouting of a seed.
Speaking in conflict by means of those two is meant.

The counter-positions are those equal to similarity, dissimilarity, excess, deficiency, the describable, the indescribable, alternative, attainment of the probandum, non-attainment, consequence, counter-example, non-production, doubt, topic, reason, implication, non-difference, appropriateness, apprehension, non-apprehension, permanence, impermanence, and effect.
When the conclusion is drawn by similarity or dissimilarity, because the contrary of that property is also possible, these are the replies equal to similarity and dissimilarity.
Its establishment is like the establishment of a cow from cowhood.
The topic is the group of six jāti replies beginning with excess.

Because of variation in the properties of the probandum and the example, and because both would become probanda, there are the replies equal to excess, deficiency, describability, alternative, and probandum.
Since a conclusion is established from some similarity, there is no denial from dissimilarity.
And because the example is appropriate through the transfer of what is to be proved.

children.text: prāpya sādhyamaprāpya vā hetoḥ prāptyāviśiṣṭatvād aprāptyāsādhakatvācca prāptyaprāptisamau ||
children.translated_text: Whether the reason reaches the probandum or does not reach it, because in reaching it there is no distinction, and because in not reaching it it is not a prover, there are the replies equal to attainment and non-attainment.
There is no denial, because the production of pots and the like is observed, and because in pressing there is ritual harm.
Because the cause of the example is not specified, and because there is counter-establishment by a counter-example, there are the replies equal to consequence and counter-example.
Its cessation is like the avoidance of the unwanted consequence of taking up a lamp.
And when the counter-example functions as the reason, the example is not a non-reason.
The reply called 'equal to non-production' is: before production there is non-production because the cause is absent.
Since it is so, and since the cause is available for what has arisen, there is no denial of the cause.
When the universal and the example are alike in being perceptible by the senses, there is the reply called 'equal to doubt,' because of a similarity with both the eternal and the non-eternal.

children.text: sādharmyātsaṃśaye na saṃśayo vaidharmyādubhayathā vā saṃśaye 'tyantasaṃśayaprasaṅgo nityatvānabhyupagamācca sāmānyasyāpratiṣedhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If doubt arises from similarity, then because of dissimilarity there is no doubt; or, if doubt arises in both ways, there follows absolute doubt. And because the eternality of the universal is not admitted, there is no refutation.
Because the procedure is established through similarity on both sides, this is the reply called 'equal to the topic under discussion.'
The refutation is not justified, because the topic under discussion is established from the opposing side, since the opposing side too is possible.
Because the reason is not established in the three times, this is the reply called 'equal to a non-reason.'
No; because the probandum is established from the reason, the establishment of the three times is not required.
And because the refutation is not justified, there is no refutation of what is to be refuted.
Because the opposing thesis is established by presumption, this is the reply called 'equal to presumption.'

children.text: anuktasyārthāpatteḥ pakṣahāner upapattir anuktatvād anaikāntikatvāc cārthāpatteḥ ||
children.translated_text: For what has not been stated, presumption entails abandonment of one's thesis; and because it is unstated and because presumption is inconclusive, it is admissible.
If there is no distinction merely because one property is present, then the consequence would be that nothing is distinct from anything, since existence itself is present.
This is the reply called 'equal to non-distinction.'
Because a property is absent in one case and present in another, there is no refutation.
Because a reason for the establishment of both sides is possible, this is the reply called 'equal to establishment.'
There is no refutation, because one admits the reason for establishment.
Even when the specified cause is absent, because the object is perceived, this is the reply called 'equal to perception.'
There is no refutation, because that property may also be accounted for by another cause.
When absence is established from the non-perception of that, because that non-perception itself is not perceived, the contrary is possible; this is the reply called 'equal to non-perception.'
Non-perception is not a reason, because non-perception has the nature of non-apprehension.
And inwardly, the varieties of cognition make known both existence and nonexistence.
Because, from similarity, a like property is present, the consequence that everything is impermanent gives the reply called 'equal to impermanence.'
Because similarity is not established, the refutation is not established; and also because there is similarity with what is to be refuted.

children.text: dṛṣṭānte ca sādhyasādhanabhāvena prajñātasya dharmasya tasya cobhayathā bhāvānnāviśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And in the example, since the property known as standing in the relation of probandum and proof exists in both ways, there is no non-distinction.
Because the eternal has the condition of the non-eternal, and because eternality is possible in what is non-eternal, this is the reply called 'equal to eternality.'
Because what is to be refuted, though eternal, has the condition of the non-eternal, and because non-eternality is possible in what is non-eternal, there is no refutation.
Because what is produced by effort is manifold, this is the reply called 'equal to the product.'
If products are different, effort is not a reason, because the cause of non-perception may be available.
Even in the refutation, the same fault applies.
Thus in every case.
In the counter-refutation of a refutation, there is a fault like the fault in the refutation.

children.text: pratiṣedhaṃ sadoṣamabhyupetya pratiṣedhavipratiṣedhe samāno doṣaprasaṅgo matānujñā ||
children.translated_text: When, after accepting that the refutation is faulty, one makes a counter-refutation of the refutation, the consequence of the same fault is concession to the opponent's view.

children.text: svapakṣalakṣaṇāpekṣopapattyupasaṃhāre hetunirdeśe parapakṣadoṣābhyupagamāt samāno doṣa iti ||
children.translated_text: When, in concluding an establishment that depends on the definition of one's own side and in stating the reason, one admits a fault in the opponent's side, the fault is the same: so it is said.

children.text: pratijñāhāniḥ pratijñāntaraṃ pratijñāvirodhaḥ pratijñāsaṃnyāso hetvantaram arthāntaraṃ nirarthakam avijñātārtham apārthakam aprāptakālaṃ nyūnam adhikaṃ punaruktam ananubhāṣaṇam ajñānam apratibhā vikṣepo matānujñā paryanuyojyopekṣaṇaṃ niranuyojyānuyogo 'pasiddhānto hetvābhāsāśca nigrahasthānāni ||
children.translated_text: Abandonment of the thesis, change to another thesis, contradiction of the thesis, renunciation of the thesis, another reason, another subject, meaningless speech, unintelligible speech, incoherent speech, speech out of proper order, deficiency, excess, repetition, failure to restate, ignorance, lack of ready reply, evasion, concession to the opponent's view, neglecting what should be challenged, charging what should not be challenged, deviation from an accepted doctrine, and fallacious reasons are the occasions for defeat.
Abandonment of the thesis is the admission, in one's own example, of the property belonging to the counter-example.
When, because of a distinction in the property that refutes the stated object of the thesis, one specifies that object differently, that is change to another thesis.
Contradiction between the thesis and the reason is contradiction of the thesis.
When the side is refuted, withdrawing the object stated in the thesis is renunciation of the thesis.
When an undifferentiated reason has been refuted and one wants a qualification, that is another reason.
A meaning unconnected with the matter at hand is another subject.
Meaningless speech is like the mere statement of a sequence of phonemes.
What is not understood even after being stated three times to the assembly and the opponent is unintelligible speech.
Because there is no relation of prior and later, a meaning that is unconnected is incoherent speech.
Stating the members of an inference in reverse order is speech out of proper order.
What is lacking even one of the members is deficiency.
What has an extra reason or example is excess.
Restating a word or a meaning is repetition, except in the case of explanatory restatement.
But in explanatory restatement there is no repetition, because repeated wording may account for a special meaning.
Restating in explicit words what has already followed from the meaning is repetition.

children.text: vijñātasya pariṣadā trir abhihitasyāpi apratyuccāraṇam ananubhāṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Failure to repeat what has been understood by the assembly, even after it has been stated three times, is failure to restate.
Not understanding is ignorance.
Non-apprehension of an answer is lack of ready reply.
Breaking off the discussion because of preoccupation with another task is evasion.
Because one admits a fault in one's own side, the consequence of that fault in the opponent's side is concession to the opponent's view.
Not defeating someone who has reached an occasion for defeat is neglecting what should be challenged.
Alleging an occasion for defeat where there is no occasion for defeat is charging what should not be challenged.
Having accepted a doctrine, taking up the discussion without observing its rules is deviation from an accepted doctrine.
And the fallacious reasons are as previously stated.
